assumptions: SPEC-049's frozen protocol (D1-D7) stays unchanged and is amended by reference only. SPEC-082 supplies a corpus of 20-50 real-failure tasks with lineage, a private held-out split and an infrastructure-error classification. Trials are run by SPEC-084 or the existing laboratory under their own admission; this spec runs none. The power note assumes a between-task standard deviation of paired differences of 0.3; no data estimates it yet.
compatibility: Additive. SPEC-049 frozen values, harness_evaluation.py and harness_promotion.py unchanged; new record formats braid-harness-regression-registration/v0.1 and braid-harness-regression-report/v0.1 are proposals until reviewed; the read-only CLI view is extended, no write command is added. Rollback by reverting the documentation PR or removing the additive offline module.
domain: Paired regression comparisons of one baseline and one candidate harness hash on a registered SPEC-082 task corpus, split and pinned profile, plus descriptive capability reports.
execution_contract: None. executionAuthorization is false. The protocol computes verdicts from sealed records and trial outcome records; it launches, grants, promotes and activates nothing. A verdict is evidence for a human promotion decision (SPEC-085), not authority.
hypotheses: H1: on 20-50 tasks with at least 5 trials per task per arm, the regression gate reaches a noninferior or inferior verdict for most candidates. H2: task-clustered intervals are wider than trial-level intervals on real harness data. Either may fail; an inconclusive or negative result is a valid result and blocks promotion.
observation_contract: Per-trial outcome records (success, failure, infrastructure error, missing) as classified by SPEC-082 and the registered verifier, bound by hash to the sealed registration; hashes bind bytes, not authenticity or grader correctness.

scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record (evidence/t001-owner-review.md; evidence/t002-codex-review.json): command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: OD-1 to OD-6 are decided or deferred in a dated record and the spec is accepted, amended or rejected.

requirements.text: Owner review. The owner reviews this spec and plan before implementation.

scenarios.given: a capability report and a SPEC-049 protocol hash
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record (evidence/t007.json; evidence/t008-crossref.json): command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: it refuses with "no regression verdict" and the SPEC-049 protocol hash is unchanged.

requirements.text: Two classes, amendment by reference. Every report names its class (`capability` or `regression`). Only a regression verdict can support a move to `candidate` or `adopted` (SPEC-085). SPEC-049 frozen text and values stay as they are.

scenarios.given: records with a missing field, a seal time after the first trial start, or a field changed after sealing
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record (evidence/t006.json; evidence/t009-registration.json): command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: each is refused with the failing field named.

requirements.text: Sealed pre-registration. A regression record fixes, before the first trial starts: baseline and candidate hashes, the SPEC-082 corpus manifest hash and split, the task list hash, trials per task, margin δ, α, estimand, uncertainty method, cluster level, missing-outcome rule, infrastructure-error threshold and rerun limit, the pinned profile, stopping rules and the reported k values. Its SHA-256 seals it. Any later change needs a new record.

scenarios.given: trials where a task ran in one arm only, a profile differs between arms, a run id repeats, or a task is outside the held-out split
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record (evidence/t006.json): command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: the comparison is marked `invalid` with the cause.

requirements.text: Paired design on a held-out split. Baseline and candidate run the same tasks with the same trial count (at least 5 per task per arm), the same pinned model, effort, resources and host, and fresh run ids (SPEC-082). Gate tasks come from the SPEC-082 private held-out split.

scenarios.given: a fixture with hand-computed Δ and bound, and a control where trial-level errors would pass but clustered errors do not
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record (evidence/t004-fixtures.json; evidence/t006.json): command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: the values match within 10⁻⁶ and the control is not `noninferior`.

requirements.text: Estimand and clustered uncertainty. Δ = mean over tasks of (candidate success rate − baseline success rate). The primary bound is the one-sided (1 − α) lower bound from the task-clustered standard error, t distribution on T − 1 degrees of freedom. A clustered bootstrap (resample tasks, recorded seed) is a sensitivity check. Trial-level standard errors are never used.

scenarios.given: one fixture per region (noninferior, inferior, inconclusive, invalid, blocked)
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record (evidence/t006.json; evidence/t010-verdict.json): command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: each gets its verdict and only `noninferior` is marked promotion-eligible.

requirements.text: Decision rule. `noninferior` if the lower bound > −δ; `inferior` if the one-sided (1 − α) upper bound < −δ; otherwise `inconclusive`. `invalid` covers protocol breaks (REQ-004, REQ-008). A declared-effect, authority or containment violation is `blocked` whatever the statistic. Clause zero: `inconclusive` is a valid result, and it blocks promotion like `inferior`, `invalid` and `blocked`.

scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record (evidence/t006.json): command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: pass@k and pass^k match the formulas and a k greater than n is refused, not extrapolated.

requirements.text: pass@k and pass^k. Per task and arm, with n trials and c successes, report pass@k = 1 − C(n−c, k)/C(n, k) (capability) and pass^k = C(c, k)/C(n, k) (reliability) for each registered k ≤ n, then their task means with clustered intervals. Both classes report them; neither is a verdict.

scenarios.given: trials with infrastructure errors below and above the threshold
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record (evidence/t006.json; evidence/t010-verdict.json): command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: none counts as a failure, all appear in the infrastructure table, and the over-threshold case is `invalid`.

requirements.text: Infrastructure errors. Trials that SPEC-082 classifies as infrastructure errors count as neither success nor failure and are reported per arm. They may be rerun with a fresh run id up to the registered limit; a task's rate uses its valid trials. A per-arm rate or between-arm difference above the threshold is `invalid`.

scenarios.given: a fixture with missing candidate outcomes
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record (evidence/t006.json; evidence/t010-verdict.json): command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: the primary verdict uses the worst case and the three bounds are reported.

requirements.text: Missing outcomes. In the primary analysis a missing non-infrastructure outcome (ungraded, not attempted, interrupted) is a candidate failure and a baseline success. The report adds complete-case and best-case bounds and says if they differ.

scenarios.given: 19 tasks, or 20 tasks with 4 registered trials on one
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record (evidence/t006.json; evidence/t009-registration.json): command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: no verdict is issued and the report says `descriptive-only`.

requirements.text: Minimum sample and power note. A verdict needs T ≥ 20 tasks and 5 registered trials per task per arm. Each record states its power assumption (between-task spread of differences, δ, α, T). Below the minimum it is descriptive.

scenarios.given: a request to compute a verdict before all trials end, and a run stopped by a quota cap
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record (evidence/t006.json; evidence/t010-verdict.json): command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: the first is refused and the second is recorded `inconclusive` with the stop cause.

requirements.text: Stopping rules. The verdict is computed once, after all registered trials end or a registered stop fires (SPEC-049 D6 conditions, quota caps, infrastructure threshold). A stopped run is `inconclusive` or `invalid` and stays on record; a rerun is a new registration.

scenarios.given: a `noninferior` verdict on fewer than the D3 number of independent lineages
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record (evidence/t006.json; evidence/t007.json): command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: the check refuses it and the report shows the bounded claim text.
scenarios.when: a superiority claim is drafted from it

requirements.text: Claim boundary. A `noninferior` verdict reads "no worse than the baseline by more than δ on this corpus, split and profile". Utility or superiority claims keep the D3 lineage minimum.

scientific_limits: A noninferior verdict holds only for the registered corpus, split, profile and margin; it is not a utility or superiority claim, which keeps the SPEC-049 D3 lineage minimum. Tasks from one lineage are correlated; the cluster level (OD-3) bounds independence. The power figures are illustrative under an assumed spread and a normal approximation. Repeated gating on one held-out split erodes it. Structural and unit checks of the module do not prove statistical validity. A Codex review is independent model review, not human review or approval.
scope: Documentation-only amendment by reference of the SPEC-049 evaluation protocol: capability evals (pass@k, descriptive) and regression evals (paired non-inferiority gate with a pre-registered margin, at least 5 trials per task, task-clustered errors, pass^k and pass@k, infrastructure errors excluded and reported, missing-outcome sensitivity, minimum sample, power note and stopping rules). No implementation, registration or trial in the first PR.
